audit.whatIsWrong: The page reads as a hard lane (diffRating 7/10, 'Tricky matchup', Akshan winning two stages) while the data has Trundle at 54.97% over 191 games. The Level 4-5 stage is also handed to Akshan on the strength of Heroic Swing, but the actual reason he wins that window is Avengerang poke at 850 range against a 300-range Chomp.
audit.why: Trundle's only gap-closer is walking with Frozen Domain's move speed; Akshan's Q outranges everything Trundle has. That is a ranged-poke problem, not a mobility problem, and it is why the mid-levels are his.
audit.corrected: Left the ratings alone (see notes — diff/diffRating disagree across the whole champion) but re-anchored the Level 3-5 text to Avengerang range plus Heroic Swing's 18s cooldown.

audit.why: The four spikes (Chomp level 1, Subjugate at 6, Trinity Force, Akshan's first item) are the right four. Subjugate at 6 into a low-resist ranged champion is genuinely the flip point.
audit.corrected: Added Heroic Swing's 18s cooldown so the 'bait it then commit' advice has a timer on it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup-defining interaction is absent and the page actively advises the opposite. Heroic Swing 'fires a grappling hook into terrain then swings around it' — Pillar of Ice IS terrain. Telling the player to 'Land Pillar of Ice behind Akshan to cut off his retreat' hands him an anchor point in the middle of an open lane and gives him an escape he otherwise could not have had. Separately, early claims Pillar has a 'knockup'; Riot's text gives impassable terrain plus a slow, no knockup.
audit.why: Riot's Heroic Swing text: 'fires a grappling hook into terrain then swings around it... gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain.' Riot's Pillar of Ice text: 'creates an ice pillar at target location, becoming impassable terrain'. Both halves matter: the pillar can anchor him, and a pillar dropped into an already-flying swing collides and drops him.
audit.corrected: Reversed the pillar advice — never wall him in open lane, place it inside his swing arc to collide him off it. Removed the fabricated knockup. Added that Comeuppance is stopped by the first minion in the line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heroic Swing is named as the thing to track five separate times without ever stating how long it is down.
audit.why: Heroic Swing is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12 and Comeuppance is 100/85/70. Eighteen seconds is long enough to walk him down twice with Frozen Domain up.
audit.corrected: 18s and 100s now stated in the cooldown block and the report.

edits.before: Chomp is your level-1 identity — bite Akshan on every last-hit attempt, steal a chunk of his AD, and let the minion deaths heal you back up through King's Tribute. He cannot out-sustain that equation at level 1, so make him pay just for showing up. At level 2, drop Frozen Domain between you and Akshan any time he tries to kite: your movement speed on the ice closes distance faster than he expects, and the attack speed stacks let you land two or three Chomp-enhanced autos before he can disengage cleanly. Level 3 is where he pulls ahead temporarily — Heroic Swing comes online as a full escape tool, and his Q Avengerang poke starts stacking up. Drop Pillar behind his likely escape vector before you commit so the knockup and slow force him through your W zone instead of out of it; do not run a bare Chomp at a live Heroic Swing.
edits.after: Chomp is your level-1 identity — bite Akshan on every last-hit attempt, sap a chunk of his AD, and let the minion deaths heal you back through King's Tribute. He cannot out-sustain that equation at level 1, so make him pay just for showing up. At level 2, drop Frozen Domain between you and Akshan any time he tries to kite: your movement speed on the ice closes distance faster than he expects, and the attack speed lets you land two or three autos around a Chomp before he disengages. Level 3 is where he pulls ahead — Heroic Swing arrives at 18s and Avengerang out-ranges your 300-range bite. Never wall him off with Pillar of Ice: it is terrain, and his swing anchors to terrain, so a pillar in open lane is a free escape. Put it inside his swing arc instead — terrain collision drops him mid-flight.

edits.before: Pillar closes the kit — use it behind Akshan to deny disengage, or between you and Heroic Swing to break his pattern.
edits.after: Pillar closes the kit, but it is terrain and Heroic Swing anchors to terrain — place it inside his arc, never as a wall.

edits.after: - Akshan Heroic Swing: 18s at rank 1 — it anchors to terrain, so never hand him a Pillar in open lane. - Comeuppance: 100s.
